scope: Theorem 6.1 (Type II distribution) of the manuscript “Prime Predecessors with an Even Number of Prime Factors” (preprints/Prime-Predecessors-with-an-Even-Number-of-Prime-Factors-September-17-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 011 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8ee2d8f79198dd5f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix D∗, b∗, C > 0. Let U, V be dyadic scales such that UV ≍ x, xb∗ ≤ U, V ≤ x1−b∗ , and let K ⊂ [U, 2U) and J ⊂ [V, 2V ) be intervals. Suppose |αm|, |βn| ≤ LC and αm = 0 unless P−(m) > W. There is a fixed B, depending only on these fixed data and on the fixed weight and cutoff data, for which the following holds. Assume that the sequence αm1m∈K satisfies (4.6); explicitly, assume X m∈I αm1m∈Kχ(m)m−1+it ≤ L−B I ⊂ [1, x2] an interval, mod(χ) ≤ LB, |t| ≤ LB ! . (6.1) Then X m∈K, n∈J, u≥1 mn=2u+1 αmβnA(u)Ψ(u/x) ≪ xL−D∗ . (6.2) The estimate is uniform in the intervals and coefficient sequences satisfying these assumptions. No discrepancy or smoothness assumption is imposed on β.
